taglines: It's Sunday and somewhere between last night and this morning you made a decision that you're calling 'self-care' but which is more accurately described as 'refusing to exist at full capacity until forced to.'
The to-do list from Thursday is still technically open in a tab. It is load-bearing at this point. Closing it would mean acknowledging what week it is.

You woke up with an idea so good you immediately suspected you'd heard it somewhere before and spent forty minutes searching to confirm you hadn't. You hadn't. This is the most productive thing you've done all week.

Sunday is the day the brain performs a slow audit of every email you didn't send, every thing you said that landed wrong, and every minor administrative task you have deferred since March. It is not a restful process.

Somewhere right now someone is 'pivoting' their 'personal brand' on LinkedIn and writing about how their biggest professional lesson is 'vulnerability.' You have blocked this person and you're a better thinker for it.

The thing you've been putting off is not actually that bad. You know this because you've now spent more time thinking about not doing it than doing it would have ever taken. This observation will not motivate you to do it.

Coffee is good. Hot coffee is better. Coffee that's been sitting on your desk for two hours while you were in the zone on something is technically still coffee. You've made worse decisions. You'll drink it.

A Sunday with no agenda is theoretically liberating and in practice deeply unsettling. Humans were not designed for total freedom. We were designed for mild inconvenience and a clear sense of what's expected of us.
